title: Cyclic dependency pyspark repository palantir
question:
I have an issue with PySpark in Palantir Foundry Repository.

I have a table X, which is derived from Y after some processing. Now, I want to replace Y with X, but the repository check detects a cyclic dependency error, as expected.

I've tried everything:

Creating a third table identical to X and replacing Y with it.

Using checkpointing.

Nothing works because the check itself fails before execution.

I also tried exporting it as a CSV and re-importing it, but the file is too large.

Any suggestions?
answer:
You have Y => X and you want to replace it for X => X ?

From a structural perspective, reading and writing to the same dataset isn't allowed (as in having it as input AND output), because it is a cycle. So there won't be a way to achieve it, at least not by having the same dataset as input AND output of the same transform.

If you want to read and write in the same dataset, you can just add it as an output, and make the transform incremental. This will give you the option to read from it too. So <nothing> => X, like:

@incremental()
@transform( my_dataset_output = Output(...) )
def compute(...)
 df = my_dataset_output.dataframe()
 my_dataset_output.write_dataframe(df)

If you goal is to do a one-off change (e.g. to do X => Z, but you want to keep the same transform in the middle), you will need to "disconnect" the transform from its current output. In other words, if you want to change "which transform will output this dataset" you need to change it's "attribution".

To do so, you can go in the details of the output dataset and delete the "jobspecs" of this dataset. You might get multiple warnings and that's legitimate given that will prevent your dataset from building, until a new code repo takes its ownership.

Jobspecs are basically a way to "define where this dataset comes from (repository, commit, etc.)". Hence by deleting the jobspecs, you break this link and the dataset won't "know" how to be built anymore.

From there, you can write a new transform, that will output to the same dataset path/rid and the checks should pass.
